evals.prompt: I'm the freelance SEO consultant for «Ελιά & Θυμάρι» (elia-thymari.gr), a small Cretan online deli — olive oil, thyme honey, herb blends. The two founders report monthly to a Dutch investor couple, so the report has to be in English. I hand-transcribed our Search Console and GA4 exports for June and July 2026 into evals/files/gsc-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md and evals/files/analytics-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md — no tools are connected in this session; those two files are the entire data set. My retainer plus content costs run €900/month all-in. Build the July 2026 monthly performance report versus June for the investor audience: traffic, search performance, conversions and revenue, SEO ROI, technical health from the developer's PageSpeed hand-check in the analytics file, and whatever the other report sections honestly support from this data.
evals.expected_output: A July-vs-June investor report built solely from the two hand-transcribed fixtures: configuration and metrics-at-a-glance per the templates, deltas computed correctly (sessions +21.4%, clicks +25.6%, impressions +40.0%, purchases +15.2%) with the GA4 and GSC populations kept apart, CTR and conversion rate per the kpi-definitions formulas (4.00%→3.59%; 1.93%→1.83%), July SEO ROI ≈ +129% from the €900 spend with the 12-month-horizon caveat, the PageSpeed check judged on the R4 thresholds (LCP 2.8 s not yet Good, INP 190 ms and CLS 0.08 Good, no FID), CITE/CORE-EEAT/backlink/AI sections honestly marked not evaluated, and every figure source-labeled user-provided with zero invented numbers.
expectations: The report opens with the skill's configuration and executive-summary shape per the report-output templates: domain elia-thymari.gr, report period July 2026, comparison period June 2026, and the executive/investor audience stated, plus a key-metrics-at-a-glance table showing July and June values side by side with a change column.

Period-over-period deltas are computed correctly from the two fixture months and within rounding: organic sessions 2,380 → 2,890 (+21.4%), GSC clicks 2,000 → 2,512 (+25.6%), impressions 50,000 → 70,000 (+40.0%), and organic purchases 46 → 53 (+15.2%) — with GA4 sessions and GSC clicks kept as two distinct metrics from two distinct sources (a report that presents the 2,512 clicks as 'organic sessions/visits', or otherwise swaps the sessions/users/clicks populations, fails).

Ratio KPIs follow the kpi-definitions formulas with their populations intact: organic CTR = clicks ÷ impressions × 100 (4.00% June → 3.59% July, never computed from sessions), and organic conversion rate = organic purchases ÷ organic sessions × 100 (1.93% June → 1.83% July, never computed from clicks or from all-channel sessions).

SEO ROI uses the kpi-definitions formula ((organic revenue − SEO investment) ÷ investment × 100) with the prompt's €900/month investment and the fixture's €2,060 July organic revenue — ≈ +129% for July, derivation visible — and carries kpi-definitions' note that SEO ROI is properly measured over 12+ month horizons so a single-month figure is directional; computing revenue ÷ investment without subtracting the investment, or presenting monthly ROI with no horizon caveat, fails.

The technical-health section judges the developer's PageSpeed hand-check against exactly the Core Web Vitals Good thresholds LCP ≤2.5s, INP ≤200ms, CLS ≤0.1 (settled ruling R4, docs/loop/SETTLED-RULINGS.md): July mobile LCP 2.8 s reported as improved from 3.1 s but still not Good (>2.5–4.0 s = needs improvement; the middle band's lower bound is exclusive per kpi-definitions.md — a value of exactly 2.5 s, 200 ms or 0.1 is Good and nothing else), INP 190 ms as Good (down from June's 205 ms, which sat above the 200 ms line), CLS 0.08 as Good — values carried with units and scoped to the one tested page (homepage, mobile, lab values), with FID never presented as a live metric and no substitute thresholds used.

Report sections whose data the fixtures do not contain are scoped honestly per the skill's own notes: domain authority / CITE marked 'Not yet evaluated', content quality / CORE-EEAT marked not yet evaluated, and backlinks, rankings beyond the GSC position averages, AI citations, and competitive standing reported as no data available — naming what would supply them — rather than filled in.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every number in the report traces to the two fixtures or the prompt, or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., the month-over-month % changes computed from the two fixture months), each data point is source-labeled as the consultant's hand-transcribed user-provided exports per the skill's source discipline (never presented as live tool-fetched), and no year-over-year figures, targets, industry benchmarks passed off as measurements, or third-party metrics are invented.

evals.prompt: I look after marketing at Ελιά & Θυμάρι (elia-thymari.gr). Our overall Search Console CTR fell from 4.0% in June to about 3.6% in July, and our investor group read that as 'the six new guide articles launched in late June backfired — the snippets must be getting worse'; one investor wants the guides taken down. Before anyone does that: the full segmented Search Console transcription is in evals/files/gsc-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md — no tools connected, that file is everything we have. Write the search-performance section of the July report: what actually happened to CTR and average position, and your recommendation on the guides.
evals.expected_output: A search-performance section that clears the guides: overall CTR 4.00%→3.59% reproduced as clicks÷impressions, the fall explained as impression-mix shift (non-brand share of impressions 80.0%→87.1%) while every pre-existing segment's CTR rose (brand 12.0%→13.0%, established non-brand 2.0%→2.3%) and the new cluster entered at 1.96% from position 14.9 — inside the position-band CTR benchmark — the site-wide average-position rise 5.68→7.98 explained as the impression-weighted effect of the new cluster, removal not supported by the data, outside causes offered only as labeled hypotheses (the fixture's dashboard note rules out a core update in-window), and nothing beyond fixture arithmetic.
expectations: CTR figures are fixture-exact with the population defined as GSC clicks ÷ impressions per month: overall 4.00% June (2,000/50,000) → 3.59% July (2,512/70,000 — the prompt's '3.6%'), brand 12.0% → 13.0%, non-brand established 2.0% → 2.3%, and the new guides cluster entering at 1.96% — with sessions or users never substituted into any CTR computation.

The mix-shift is named as the explanation: the section states that every segment that existed in June improved its CTR while the overall CTR fell, because the impression mix shifted toward structurally lower-CTR non-brand queries — non-brand share of total impressions 80.0% (40,000/50,000) → 87.1% (61,000/70,000), the new cluster alone contributing 18,000 of July's 70,000 impressions — consistent with kpi-definitions' rule to always separate brand vs non-brand; a diagnosis that site-wide snippets/titles got worse (the investors' reading) fails.

Average position is handled per kpi-definitions ('a directional indicator, not an absolute measure … pair with keyword distribution'): the site-wide impression-weighted average moving 5.68 → 7.98 is explained by the new cluster entering at position 14.9 while brand held 1.2 and non-brand established improved 6.8 → 6.5 — reading the site-wide rise as existing rankings collapsing fails.

The take-the-guides-down question is answered from the fixture: the six new articles added 353 July clicks at 1.96% CTR from average position 14.9 — at or above kpi-definitions' expected 0.5–2% CTR band for positions 11–20 — so the data does not support removal; and any cause offered beyond the fixture (a core or spam update — which the fixture's Search Status Dashboard note rules out as a *listed* update for this window; broader unannounced algorithm volatility, SERP features, AI Overviews, seasonality) appears only as an explicitly labeled hypothesis naming its confirming check, never as an asserted finding.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every click, impression, CTR, position, and share figure traces to the fixture or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., the 80.0% → 87.1% impression shares), count populations stay labeled throughout (clicks vs impressions vs share of impressions), the section is labeled as user-provided transcription, and no search volumes, sessions, revenue, SERP-feature data, or competitor figures appear.

evals.prompt: GEO update for elia-thymari.gr. On 26 June I reworked our flagship olive-oil guide (/odigoi/elaiolado-odigos) for AI answers — answer-first opening, sourced stats table, cleaner headings. The founders now see AI-assistant referrals roughly doubled in July and want to tell the investors 'the GEO rework doubled our AI traffic.' My GA4 referral drilldown and page-level cut are in evals/files/ai-referrals-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md, and the channel totals in evals/files/analytics-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md — no tools connected; those transcriptions are all the data. Build the AI-referral section of the July report: the headline AI share, sessions by assistant, the landing-page cut, conversions — and tell me straight whether we can put that causal claim in front of the board.
evals.expected_output: An AI-referral cut per the skill's 5b template: headline AI share of total sessions 1.23%→2.04% (50→95 sessions, +90%), sessions by roster assistant only (skroutz.gr and the forum excluded from every AI figure), the board's causal claim converted to delta-vs-control (+194.4% reworked guide vs +33.3% untouched holdout, ≈161pp gap) with the same-week new-cluster confound acknowledged and consistent-with language instead of proof, the linked-not-cited caveat with citation checking as the named next step, GSC AI-surface carried as not exposed, the engagement row left unfilled, AI conversion rates from fixture purchases only, and everything labeled hand-transcribed user-provided.
expectations: The headline follows the skill's AI-referrals cut: AI referral sessions 50 → 95 (+90%) and AI share of total sessions 1.23% → 2.04% (≈ +0.8pp), where the share's denominator is all-channel total sessions from the analytics fixture (4,072 June / 4,664 July) — a share computed against referral-channel sessions only (310/356) or against organic sessions fails.

The count rule is stated and applied: AI referral sessions = sessions whose session source matches the kpi-definitions AI hostname roster — here chatgpt.com (29→58), perplexity.ai (12→22), copilot.microsoft.com (6→10), and claude.ai (3→5) — while skroutz.gr, pagkritio-forum.gr, and the aggregated other referral sources are never counted into any AI figure, and the roster is treated as operational matching config (echoing its churn/[VERIFY] caveat is a plus; asserting roster completeness as fact fails).

The board claim is answered with the skill's control rule: attribution is reported as delta-vs-control — reworked guide +194.4% (18→53 AI sessions) against the untouched honey-guide holdout +33.3% (15→20), a gap of ≈161pp (194.4 − 33.3 = 161.1pp) — never as the raw doubling alone, the same-week confound (six new guide articles launched 24–26 June) is acknowledged, and causal language stays at consistent-with/supports rather than asserting 'the rework caused/doubled it' as established fact.

The linked-not-cited caveat is carried in substance alongside any win claim: AI referral traffic proves an AI answer linked the site, not that it cited it prominently, and referrals are treated as leads for citation checking (an ~~AI monitor pass or manual assistant checks being the named next step), not as citation proof.

The GSC AI-surface corroboration slot carries the fixture's actual state — 'not exposed for this property' — with no simulated Search Console AI-surface rows, and every figure is labeled as the consultant's hand-transcribed user-provided GA4 data per the skill's tool-measured/user-provided/estimated label discipline, never presented as live tool-fetched.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every session and purchase count traces to the two fixtures or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., AI conversion rates 1/50 = 2.0% June and 3/95 ≈ 3.2% July, computed as AI-referral purchases ÷ AI-referral sessions), the template's engagement-rate row is omitted or marked not-transcribed rather than filled (the fixture says engagement was not pulled), and no citation counts, citation positions, or answer-coverage figures appear (the fixture states no ~~AI monitor data exists).

evals.prompt: Board request for elia-thymari.gr: our investor group meets Thursday and asked for the Q3 2026 quarterly report with a quarter-over-quarter table against Q2. Today is 10 August 2026. Everything we have is the June and July hand-transcriptions in evals/files/gsc-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md and evals/files/analytics-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md — no tools connected. Please produce the Q3 report with the QoQ comparison; if some numbers are missing, just work with what's there and make it look complete.
evals.expected_output: An honest scope correction instead of a fabricated quarter: Q3 has one of its three months on file (July) and the requested Q2 baseline one of three (June), so no quarterly totals or QoQ percentages appear as actuals despite the make-it-look-complete pressure; the report delivers what the data supports — July-vs-June month-over-month (+21.4% sessions, +25.6% clicks, +15.2% purchases) framed as month one of Q3 — names the missing exports (August/September; April/May for Q2), schedules the real Q3 report after 30 September, and keeps the configuration block and no-data sections truthful.
expectations: The data gap is named with its count rule before any numbers: Q3 2026 spans July+August+September and the fixtures cover 1 of those 3 months (July complete; August under way as of the prompt's 10 August; September in the future), while the requested Q2 baseline has only 1 of its 3 months (June — April and May absent), so neither quarter can be reported as measured.

No quarterly figures are fabricated despite the 'make it look complete' pressure: no Q3 or Q2 totals and no quarter-over-quarter percentages appear as actuals (no July×3 run-rate passed off as the quarter, no projected August/September values inside a QoQ table), any forward projection appears only if unmistakably labeled as a projection from one month of data, and declining the requested QoQ table IS the passing behavior.

The honestly scoped alternative is delivered from the data that exists: a July-vs-June month-over-month report (organic sessions 2,380 → 2,890 +21.4%, GSC clicks 2,000 → 2,512 +25.6%, organic purchases 46 → 53 +15.2%) framed as the first month of Q3, with the true quarterly report scheduled after 30 September and the missing inputs named (August and September exports; April and May for any Q2 baseline).

The report configuration states what the report actually is per the configuration template: report period July 2026, comparison period June 2026, audience executive/board — not 'Q3 2026 vs Q2 2026' — and any quarter-to-date label is explicitly scoped to July only.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every figure traces to the two fixtures or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., the month-over-month % changes computed from the two fixture months), no August-to-date, year-over-year, target, or revenue-projection numbers are invented, and sections without fixture data (backlinks, AI citations, CITE, CORE-EEAT) stay honest per the skill's not-yet-evaluated pattern.

evals.prompt: Είμαι η Ελένη Βασιλάκη από το «Ελιά & Θυμάρι» (elia-thymari.gr). Θέλω την αναφορά Ιουλίου στα ελληνικά, για εμένα και τη συνέταιρό μου — δεν έχουμε σχέση με τα τεχνικά. Ό,τι στοιχεία έχουμε τα πέρασε με το χέρι ο σύμβουλός μας: evals/files/gsc-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md, evals/files/analytics-export-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md, evals/files/ai-referrals-elia-thymari-jun-jul.md, και το σημείωμα με τους στόχους που είχα στείλει τον Ιούνιο, evals/files/client-goals-note-elia-thymari-el.md. Κανένα εργαλείο δεν είναι συνδεδεμένο — αυτά τα τέσσερα αρχεία είναι όλα τα δεδομένα. Φτιάξε την πλήρη μηνιαία αναφορά Ιουλίου σε σύγκριση με τον Ιούνιο: πώς πήγαμε, αν πιάσαμε τους δύο στόχους μου, και τι προτείνεις για τον Αύγουστο.
evals.expected_output: A Greek client-facing July report from the four fixtures: summary, June/July metrics table (2,890 οργανικές συνεδρίες, 2,512 κλικ, 70,000 εμφανίσεις, 53 παραγγελίες, €2,060 έσοδα) with the populations kept distinct in the Greek labels, the two goals checked honestly (sessions goal met at 2,890 vs 2.800; orders goal missed at 53 of 60) quoting the owner's goal lines verbatim wherever quoted, mechanically clean Greek with zero §6 regression classes (no «Όλα τα [N]» calque, no agency placeholders in the client-facing body), ratio KPIs per kpi-definitions, unmeasured sections named as such in natural Greek, any CWV line judged on the exact R4 thresholds, no ROI computed without the missing spend input — and fluency itself routed to the binding greek-content-editor pass.
expectations: The deliverable is a client-facing July-vs-June report written in Greek in the skill's report shape — summary, key-metrics table with June and July values and change, goals check, and recommendations for August — with headline numbers fixture-exact (2,890 οργανικές συνεδρίες, 2,512 κλικ, 70,000 εμφανίσεις, 53 παραγγελίες από οργανική αναζήτηση, €2,060 οργανικά έσοδα) and the populations kept distinct in the Greek wording: συνεδρίες vs κλικ vs παραγγελίες — presenting the 2,512 GSC clicks as «επισκέψεις»/«συνεδρίες» fails. Fixture-exact means the numeric values match; either thousands convention (2,890/70,000 or 2.890/70.000) passes provided the formatting-consistency expectation is met.

Both goals from the goals note are checked honestly: the sessions goal of 2.800 (i.e. 2,800) reported as met with 2,890, and the orders goal of 60 reported as missed with 53 of 60 (−7 orders, ≈88% of target) stated plainly rather than spun as a success — and any direct quotation of the owner's goal lines reproduces them verbatim, character for character, from the note (e.g. «60 παραγγελίες από οργανική αναζήτηση μέσα στον Ιούλιο»), never a paraphrase inside quotation marks.

Greek output quality (watch-item W4 guard, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md), mechanical layer plus the binding editor's verdict: correct diacritics and final-sigma use throughout, no untranslated English boilerplate section headings (product names such as GA4, Search Console, PageSpeed and hostnames such as chatgpt.com stay in Latin script), and one number-formatting convention used consistently. This expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on this eval's Greek output (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). That grade decides fluency, idiomatic naturalness, translation-ese and register, and where any clause above names fluency, naturalness or register it decides that clause too — this grader forms no second opinion on it. PASS = the mechanical clauses above hold AND the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL, or any mechanical clause above is breached. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing.

Anti-slop §6 placement discipline (ruled Greek regression classes, build/seo-content-writer/references/anti-slop-ruleset.md): no totality-with-numeral calque anywhere (greppable pattern «Όλα τα [0-9]» — a sentence covering all six new guides uses «Και τα 6/έξι …» or a restructure), and no agency-provenance labels or placeholders inside the client-facing body (no «απαιτούνται στοιχεία…», no [CLIENT DATA…]/[SOURCE NEEDED…] tokens) — missing data is voiced as honest client-facing prose or a labeled gaps note (ledger F13 placement discipline); recurrence of a §6 FAIL-grade family is an automatic FAIL.

Ratio KPIs and thresholds keep kpi-definitions fidelity in Greek: CTR 3.59% as κλικ ÷ εμφανίσεις (2,512/70,000) and ποσοστό μετατροπής 1.83% as παραγγελίες ÷ οργανικές συνεδρίες (53/2,890) — comma or point decimals both acceptable; sections the fixtures cannot support (domain authority/CITE, CORE-EEAT, backlinks, share of voice, AI citations beyond the GA4 referral rows) are marked as not yet measured in natural Greek instead of filled; and if the report includes the PageSpeed line it judges against exactly LCP ≤2.5s / INP ≤200ms / CLS ≤0.1 with FID never presented as a live metric (settled ruling R4).

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every figure traces to the four fixtures or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., the −7-orders goal gap, the +21.4% month-over-month sessions change computed from the two fixture months), sources are described in client-appropriate Greek as the consultant's hand-entered data (never as live tool reads), and no SEO-ROI percentage is produced — the fixtures carry revenue but no investment figure, so ROI is named as needing the spend input rather than computed from an invented one.
